author: dinakartumu
body:
Closes #19.

## The pattern

Every sync service recorded its own failure like this:

```ts
} catch (err) {
  await db.update(syncRuns).set({ status: 'failed', ... })   // <- a D1 round trip
  throw err;
}
```

The bookkeeping write is itself a D1 call, so whatever killed the sync — an
exhausted subrequest budget, a killed isolate, a D1 blip — is very likely to
take it down too. When that happens:

- the secondary error escapes and **replaces the real cause**
- the row stays at `status: 'running'` **forever**
- `/v1/health/sync` reports the domain as in-progress, which reads as healthy

This is how the Trakt watch-history sync stayed broken for eleven hours on
2026-07-26 without surfacing anywhere. **416 rows** are stranded at `running`
across the table's history.

## Change

`markRunFailed` was introduced in `trakt/history-sync.ts` as a local fix. It is
not Trakt-specific, so it moves to `src/lib/sync-run.ts` and is now used by all
twelve services:

`attending/backfill` · `foursquare` · `github` · `instapaper` · `lastfm` ·
`letterboxd` · `plex` · `rescuetime` · `strava` · `trakt/history-sync` ·
`trakt/sync` · `wakatime`

Rethrow semantics are unchanged — only the bookkeeping becomes non-throwing, so
the caller's `throw err` still carries the error that matters. Strava's
`itemsSynced` (partial progress on failure) is preserved via an options
argument.

## The guard

Twelve services drifted into hand-rolling this one at a time, which is a review
problem, not a knowledge problem. So `src/lib/sync-run.test.ts` scans every
service source via `import.meta.glob` and fails if any writes `status: 'failed'`
itself. Against the unfixed tree it names all twelve.

Also covered: that `markRunFailed` swallows its own write failure, proven by
driving it with a D1 binding whose `prepare` throws `Too many subrequests`.

## Note on the complementary half

This cannot help when an isolate is hard-killed, because no application code
runs at all. That case is covered by the `stale` reporting already shipped in
`/v1/health/sync`, which flags any run still `running` past a Worker's
15-minute lifetime. The two together cover both shapes of the failure.

## Verification

```
Test Files  122 passed (122)
     Tests  1473 passed (1473)
```
`tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint` clean.

## Review note

The bulk edit was scripted, and the script got two things wrong that I caught by
reading the diff rather than trusting the run: it spliced an import into the
middle of a multi-line import block in `strava/sync.ts`, and in the two services
whose helper takes the message as a shorthand `error,` property it silently fell
back to a placeholder string, discarding the real message. Both are fixed — all
twelve call sites are listed above and forward the genuine error — but the
diff is worth a read on those two files specifically.

body:
## Summary

- **Migrate** the toolchain to [ruff 0.16.0](https://astral.sh/blog/ruff-v0.16.0) by raising the floor in the `dev` and `lint` dependency groups and relocking.
- **Adopt** ruff's curated default rule set by switching `select` to `extend-select`, taking the enabled-rule count from 351 to 565.
- **Fix** the diagnostics that adoption surfaced, and scope a per-file ignore, with its reason, for each site where the flagged construct is deliberate.
- **Format** the Python code blocks inside `README.md` and `notes/`, which `ruff format` now rewrites by default.

## Changes

### Dependencies

**pyproject.toml** raises `ruff` to `>=0.16.0` in both the `dev` and `lint` groups, and **uv.lock** moves ruff 0.15.22 to 0.16.0. A floor rather than a pin, so contributors and CI agree on the diagnostics without freezing patch releases out.

### Rule selection

ruff 0.16 ships a curated 413-rule default set as its recommended baseline. An explicit `select` **replaces** that set rather than extending it, so naming linters there silently opted the project out of everything ruff enables by default. `RuleSelector` has no `DEFAULT` token, so there is no way to name the default set from inside `select`; leaving `select` unset and listing the project's own linters under `extend-select` is the only way to get defaults-plus-extras.

**pyproject.toml** makes that switch with the same entries, one per line, each labelled with the linter it selects, and records in the file why `select` stays unset. Enabled rules go from 351 to 565.

### Lint fixes

**src/libvcs/_internal/query_list.py**, **src/libvcs/_internal/subprocess.py**, and **tests/test_shortcuts.py** move `None` to the end of their type unions ([`RUF036`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/none-not-at-end-of-union/)). Annotation-only reordering with no runtime or type-checking effect — `int | IO[Any] | None` and `None | int | IO[Any]` denote the same type. The `_FILE` alias in `subprocess.py` now matches the identically named alias in `_internal/run.py`, which already ordered `None` last.

Every exception class calls `super().__init__(...)` as a statement instead of returning it ([`PLE0101`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/return-in-init/)). `__init__` must return None; the old form read as if the base initializer produced a value worth propagating.

`ProgressCallbackProtocol` receives an aware UTC `datetime` rather than a naive local one ([`DTZ005`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/call-datetime-now-without-tzinfo/)). Naive timestamps taken on hosts in different zones compared and serialized as though they named the same instant, and a DST rollover made them ambiguous on a single host. Callbacks that only format the value for display are unaffected.

`GitSubmoduleManager._ls` reads submodule name, url, and branch from `.gitmodules` directly ([`S110`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/try-except-pass/), [`BLE001`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/blind-except/)). Each lookup already passes `check_returncode=False`, which is exactly the switch that stops `run()` raising on a non-zero exit, so the `try`/`except Exception`/`pass` around it guarded a failure mode the call cannot produce while swallowing any real one.

`_TXT` is gone from `libvcs._internal.subprocess` ([`PYI047`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/unused-private-type-alias/)) — a private type alias with no annotation referencing it. The two `subprocess.run` calls in the test suite that assert on `returncode` themselves now say `check=False` ([`PLW1510`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/subprocess-run-without-check/)).

`libvcs.sync.svn` loses its `#!/usr/bin/env python` line ([`EXE001`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/shebang-not-executable/)). The module is imported, never executed — no `__main__` guard, no executable bit — so the shebang advertised an entry point that does not exist. This one is only visible on CI: ruff skips the rule on WSL, where it was authored.

### Scoped ignores

Four rules fire on constructs that are deliberate here. Each is scoped to the file it applies to, never repo-wide, with the reason recorded next to the entry in `pyproject.toml`.

[`S102`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/exec-builtin/) in **docs/conf.py**: the Sphinx config reads `__title__`, `__version__`, and friends by exec'ing `src/libvcs/__about__.py` into a dict, which keeps the docs build from importing libvcs so version metadata resolves even when the package is not installed. The exec'd file is this repository's own source.

[`PLW1509`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/subprocess-popen-preexec-fn/) in **src/libvcs/_internal/run.py**: `run()` reproduces `subprocess.Popen`'s signature so callers can reach any of it, `preexec_fn` included, and defaults it to None. libvcs never forks with a preexec hook on its own; the thread-safety hazard belongs to a caller that opts in.

[`BLE001`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/blind-except/) in **src/libvcs/_internal/query_list.py**: QueryList filters arbitrary caller-supplied objects, so resolving a `food__istartswith` path walks `__getattr__`, properties, and `__eq__` that libvcs did not write. An unresolvable lookup is a non-match, not an error — `keygetter` and `parse_lookup` log at debug and return None while the `in`/`nin` predicates return False. Narrowing the handlers would let a foreign property abort an entire filter.

[`BLE001`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/blind-except/) in **src/libvcs/sync/svn.py**: `SvnSync.url_rev` falls back to shelling out to `svn info --xml` and scraping the result when neither the `.svn/entries` nor the XML layout applies. What that can raise depends on the installed svn, the working copy layout, and the output format. The method's contract is to answer `(None, 0)` for a working copy it cannot read.

### Formatting

**README.md** and **notes/2025-11-26-command-support.md** get their Python blocks normalized: double quotes, standard argument wrapping, single-space comment gaps, trailing whitespace removed. All of it is mechanical output of `ruff format`, which in 0.16.0 descends into Markdown fences by default. `ruff format . --check` in CI fails without it.

## Design decisions

Expanding to whole prefixes instead of the curated default set was rejected: it is one to two orders of magnitude noisier, because it drags in all of `D`, `PL`, `S`, and friends rather than ruff's own recommended subset.

Each rule lands as its own commit — one per fix, one per ignore — so a disagreement over any single disposition can be reverted without unpicking the rest. Ignores carry their justification in `pyproject.toml` rather than as `# noqa` comments in the code.

The `_FILE` alias fix was applied by hand because ruff classifies it as an unsafe fix — the alias is a runtime assignment, not an annotation, so ruff cannot rule out code that inspects `typing.get_args()` ordering. Nothing in the tree does; the alias is referenced only from annotations and docstrings.

The `notes/` reformat was accepted rather than excluded from the formatter. It flattens some hand-aligned trailing comments in a design note, but carving `notes/` out of `ruff format` is a policy change that belongs in its own PR, not in a version bump.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run ruff check .` — clean
- [x] `uv run ruff format . --check` — clean
- [x] `uv run mypy` — clean
- [x] `uv run py.test` — green

The `Git.help` doctest calls `git help --all`, which intermittently hangs on the author's machine regardless of this branch: `run()` does not drain the child's pipes when no `timeout` is given, so the child blocks on write while the parent spins in its poll loop. It reproduces identically on an unmodified `master` checkout, and it is on a code path this branch does not touch. Pre-existing and out of scope here; CI is the authority on that test.

body:
## Intent

Fix dragon-math's lint configuration so server code is linted as Node rather than as browser code, then triage whatever real problems that reveals.

The problem: eslint.config.js applied globals.browser to every '**/*.{js,jsx}' file and granted globals.node only to '**/*.test.js'. The entire Express server runs on Node and uses require/module/process/__dirname, so every one of those was reported as no-undef - roughly 282 false errors out of 365 total. The confirming evidence that this was config noise and not code debt: adding two require lines during an unrelated task moved the count from 362 to 364, exactly one error per line. The real cost was never the number; it was that any GENUINE lint error in server/ was invisible under hundreds of false ones, so lint provided no value on the server at all.

What the user asked for, and the decisions made:

1. Cover all Node-executed code, inventoried rather than assumed: server/**, all *.cjs files, root build/tool configs (vite.config.js, vitest.config.js, eslint.config.js, drizzle.config.cjs), and the scripts/ helpers (both .cjs and .mjs and one ESM .js). The inventory turned up that '**/*.cjs' and '**/*.mjs' were previously matched by NO config block at all, so they were being linted with zero rules; they are now covered, which is where the single genuinely new finding came from.

2. Explicitly NOT fixing the noise by making everything permissive. The user called this out directly: granting node globals repo-wide would hide a real no-undef in frontend code, which is the one place the rule genuinely earns its keep. So the config is deliberately structured as a no-globals baseline block carrying js.configs.recommended for all JS/JSX, plus one block per runtime that opts files in: browser (src/**, solve-game.js) keeps globals.browser and the React plugins; server/**/*.js and **/*.cjs get globals.node with sourceType commonjs; Node ESM (root *.config.js, scripts/**) gets globals.node with sourceType module; the vitest block re-asserts sourceType module over the CommonJS block because the server test files are ESM. That re-assert is load-bearing, not cosmetic: server/db.test.js and server/lib/health.test.js use import.meta.url, which is a parse error under the commonjs block that server/**/*.js otherwise puts them in. The no-globals baseline is what makes this safe - a runtime block has to opt each file in, nothing is permissive by default. Verified in both directions with a throwaway probe: 'document' in a server/ file and 'process' in a src/ file each still error no-undef. The probe files were deleted and are not in the diff.

3. Report before/after counts explicitly in the PR body: 365 errors before, 80 after. All 80 remaining are pre-existing frontend findings in src/ (React hooks/refresh rules, unused vars). I diffed the per-finding list before and after and it is byte-identical, so this change neither hid nor introduced a frontend finding. Node-side lint output is now completely clean.

4. Triage what the fix revealed. Five findings surfaced, all dead code, all pure removals with no behavior change, so none needed escalation: server/lib/dragonArt.js dropped a 'let entries = []' initializer that is never read because the catch does 'continue'; server/lib/email.js had an 'eslint-disable-next-line global-require' suppressing a rule that no longer exists in ESLint core, so the dead directive was replaced with a comment explaining why the require is lazy; server/lib/schoolAdminInvite.js dropped an unused 'and' import from drizzle-orm; server/lib/weeklyReport.js dropped an unused 'parent' from the renderWeeklyReportHtml destructured param (verified the only remaining 'parent' in that function is the literal /parent URL path, and dropping a destructured property leaves callers unaffected); scripts/seed-dragon-names.mjs dropped an unused 'schema' import.

Hard constraint the user set: do not suppress instead of fixing. No blanket eslint-disable, no deleting the no-undef rule, no adding files to the ignore list to make numbers drop - every one of those shortcuts makes lint output less trustworthy while appearing to succeed. None were used. Note that REMOVING the dead global-require directive is the opposite of suppression.

Scope constraints: five other changes are in flight on this repo, so the diff is deliberately narrow - the lint config plus only the genuine lint fixes that fell out of triage. Branch was rebased onto latest main (already up to date at 797a88b). A separate task is adding CI and gates lint on a delta rather than an absolute count, so it works whether the baseline is 362 or 3; no coordination needed.

Its Tests section asserted that 'npm run lint has a large pre-existing error count (server files are linted with browser globals, so require/module/process all report no-undef)'. * Closes https://github.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGameCode/issues/176

This PR prevents units from deploying when they're still moving. The issue is most notable with the Nuke Cannon, which deploys and fires just ahead reaching its goal position (see issue).

author: larslaskowski
body:
## Summary

`UpsertVulnerabilityFindingsAsync` now builds its match lookup from **all** findings of an image version instead of the active ones only. Where several rows share a finding identity, the active row wins; among resolved rows the most recently resolved one is picked. A match against a resolved row reactivates it in place — `IsActive = true`, `ResolvedAtUtc` and `ResolvedByScanRunId` cleared, `ScanRunId` stamped with the current run and a fresh `DetectedAtUtc` for the new active period. The stale pass at the end of the upsert now iterates only over rows that were already active when the run started, so a row reactivated in the same run cannot be deactivated again.

## Why

The lookup was restricted to active findings, so an advisory that had been resolved in an earlier run and was reported again never matched. Each re-detection inserted a brand-new row while the old one stayed behind as a resolved tombstone. That grew the findings table by a full copy of the finding set per resolve/re-detect cycle — 1236 extra rows for an image with 1236 findings — until `ScanCleanupBackgroundService` passed the retention cutoff, and it reported every re-detected CVE as brand new even though it was already known.

## Linked issues

Closes #204

## Review notes

- The unique filtered index on `(ImageVersionId, AdvisoryId, AffectedPackage)` only covers active rows, so reactivation cannot collide with an existing active row for the same identity.
- Legacy duplicates already in the database need no migration; they are resolved rows and are removed by the retention cleanup. The new preference order keeps updating the active row for such identities.
- Three tests were added to `VulnerabilityEnrichmentServiceTests`: reactivation instead of insert, a reactivated row surviving the stale pass of the same run, and a legacy active/resolved pair resolving to the active row.

## Follow-up work

None

author: stasson
body:
## Why this is an E3 prerequisite, not debt

E2 shipped `ridl-backend-ts` to prove the IR is language-neutral, and then wired
it to nothing. It sat under `[dev-dependencies]` in `crates/ridlc/Cargo.toml`,
carrying the comment "the backend is a test-only dependency here"; it was
reachable from the corpus runner's snapshots and from no command. `ridlc build
--emit` offered `rust`, `c-header`, and `ir-json`.

E3's exit criterion in `docs/ROADMAP.md` is that a `view` "generates viewmodel
bindings (TS/MVVM)", and story E3.3 is "Binding codegen: viewmodel/widget
bindings (TS first)". The E2.6 row already records that E3.3 builds on it. A
binding generator whose output no command can emit does not satisfy an exit
criterion phrased as "generates", so E3.3 would have had to open by building
this path before it could build anything of its own. Doing it here keeps E3.3
about bindings. The gap is recorded on #172.

## What changed

- `crates/ridlc/Cargo.toml` — `ridl-backend-ts` moves from `[dev-dependencies]`
  to `[dependencies]`; the test-only comment is removed with it. `Cargo.lock` is
  unchanged, because a dev-dependency was already in the graph.
- `crates/ridlc/src/lib.rs` — `Emit` gains a `TypeScript` variant; `write_emits`
  gains its arm.
- `crates/ridlc/src/main.rs` — the `--emit` summary line names the fourth
  artifact.
- `crates/ridlc/tests/cli.rs` — two tests, described below.
- `docs/ROADMAP.md`, `docs/technotes/walking-skeleton-architecture.md` — both
  stated the three-value emit set as a present fact. The technote stated it
  **twice**: once in the `crates/ridlc` description and again forty lines below,
  in the end-to-end pipeline diagram, where `ridl-backend-ts` was qualified
  "(library and corpus only)". The first commit updated only the first. The
  second commit deletes the parenthetical, after twelve search patterns over
  that file and the rest of `docs/` found no third statement. `docs/archive/` is
  dated working memory and stays as written.

**Flag spelling — `typescript`.** The existing values split two ways: `rust`
names the target language, while `c-header` and `ir-json` name artifact kinds
that are not languages. The TypeScript emit is a language emit, so it takes the
language's name, as `rust` does. clap's `ValueEnum` derives kebab-case from the
variant identifier, which would give `type-script`, so the variant carries
`#[value(name = "typescript")]` and keeps the language's own casing in Rust.

**Extension — `<base>.ts`.** Forced rather than chosen **in package and
workspace mode**, where `base` is the package name: the backend emits one module
per package and writes a cross-package reference as `import * as pkg_name from
'./<package-name>';`, which resolves only against a file named
`<package-name>.ts`. It is also the name the corpus runner already writes for
its `tsc` type-check (`crates/ridlc/tests/corpus.rs`).

Single-file mode is the exception, and the second commit narrows the doc comment
to say so. There `run_build` names artifacts after the input file stem, so
`ridlc build /tmp/common.typl` for `package veh.common` writes `common.ts`, which
a sibling module importing `./veh.common` would not resolve against — confirmed
by running it. The Rust emit carries the identical asymmetry (`common.rs`), it
is deliberate, and neither is changed here.

**Not a copy of its neighbour.** `ridl_backend_ts::generate` returns
`GeneratedTs { source }` and `GenerateError::Unrepresentable(String)`, distinct
from the Rust backend's `Generated` and `GenerateError { message }`. The Rust
and C-header emits share one backend call; the TypeScript emit makes its own, so
a backend that cannot render a package skips only its own artifact. The failure
path mirrors the Rust one — a detached error diagnostic, and no file written.
The C1 gate is untouched: an error-bearing run still writes nothing.

**`crates/ridl` needed no change**, as expected. The facade re-exports
`ridlc::Emit` and forwards it, so `ridl build --emit typescript` and the value
list in `ridl build --help` both follow from the one enum. Confirmed by running
`ridl build --help` before and after the change.

The mechanism is worth stating precisely, because a first version of this
description got it wrong. It is **not** that the facade's `emit` field happens to
carry no doc comment of its own. clap renders the possible-values block from the
`ValueEnum` implementation regardless of what the field is documented with:
adding a doc comment to that field and rebuilding leaves the block byte-identical
and only prepends a summary line above it — run, diffed, reverted. So the
conclusion is stronger than a "no doc comment today" argument would support, and
no future doc comment on that field can strand the value list.

## Evidence the new tests can fail

No existing test asserted the set of accepted `--emit` values, and none
snapshotted `--help` output, so nothing needed updating; both gaps are covered
now.

`build_emit_typescript_writes_the_backend_module` runs the command, then
regenerates the expected source inside the test from the same entry through
`compile_workspace` and `ridl_backend_ts::generate`, and asserts byte equality.
Four breakages were applied to the shipped code and the resulting failures
observed:

| Break applied | Observed failure |
| --- | --- |
| `Emit::TypeScript => {}` — the arm writes nothing | `typescript writes <pkg-name>.ts: Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound, message: "No such file or directory" }` |
| the arm writes an empty `<base>.ts` | `assertion left == right failed` — `left: ""`, `right: "/**\n * @unit km/h\n ...\nexport type Speed = number & { readonly __ridl: 'veh.common.Speed' };\n..."` |
| `typescript` dropped from the `--emit` summary line | ``the --emit summary must name `typescript` `` |
| the flag value renamed to `ts` | `left: ["rust", "c-header", "ir-json", "ts"]`, `right: ["rust", "c-header", "ir-json", "typescript"]` |

All four breakages were reverted, and `crates/ridlc/tests/cli.rs` is green on
what is committed (12 tests). The byte-equality assertion is preceded by an
assertion that the expected source contains `export type Speed`, so an
empty-against-empty comparison cannot pass silently.

## Gate

Every command was run locally in the worktree, and each exited 0 — re-run in
full after the review fixes. CI confirms nothing: every run has failed without
starting a job since 2026-07-18 because of a GitHub billing state.

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `just fmt` | clean, no diff produced |
| `just check` | clean |
| `cargo test --workspace` | pass — 0 failures across every target |
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | clean (run separately) |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `just wasm-check` | clean — `ridl-backend-ts` depends only on `ridl-ir`, and the wasm gate builds `ridl-syntax`, `ridl-core`, `ridl-sem`, `ridl-ir` |
| `just verify` | pass |
| `cargo doc -p ridlc --no-deps` | warning-free, so the new intra-doc link to `run_build` resolves |

## Notes for the reviewer

**ADR-0008 is deliberately untouched, and needs a sentence changed.**
`docs/decisions/ADR-0008-e2-execution.md` states the same three-value emit set
at the end of its `## Status`, inside the third sweep's cross-check:
"`ridl-backend-ts` is a dev-dependency of `ridlc`, and `ridlc build --emit`
offers `rust`, `c-header`, and `ir-json` only. ... the missing emit path is
recorded on #172 rather than read into it here." Both halves are now false.
Editing that document means running its whole-document sweep precondition, so it
is left for a separate pass rather than half-done here.

**Overlap with the open PRs.** No file in this branch appears in #186 (justfile,
CI, `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `README.md`, `bootstrap`,
`rust-toolchain.toml`, ADR-0009) or in #187 (the book, `docs/getting-started.md`,
`crates/ridl/tests/book_examples.rs`, and the same three top-level docs).

## Summary

Prevents network crashes and silent data loss when a user pastes a comma-separated list of endpoints (e.g. `http://10.5.0.2:1234, http://localhost:1234`) into a provider Base URL settings field. Such input previously produced malformed URLs that crashed `requestUrl`/`fetch`, or silently lost all but a garbage first token.

## Changes

### Runtime sanitization (defense-in-depth, every network boundary)
- **`src/providers/provider-types.ts`** — new idempotent `sanitizeBaseUrl()` helper: keeps only the first comma-delimited entry, trims whitespace, strips trailing slashes.
- **`src/providers/base-http-provider.ts`** — constructor wraps `opts.getBaseUrl()`, so every subclass call site (endpoint builders, JIT payload decisions, `isLocalBaseUrl`/`detectLocalRuntime` checks) across all 12 HTTP providers returns sanitized values.
- **`src/providers/provider-factory.ts`** — `getBaseUrl(id)` sanitizes for direct callers like `ModelRouter.withJitModel()`.
- **`src/audio/transcriber.ts`** — `resolveConnection()` + `localRuntime()` (STT path bypasses the factory).
- **`src/main.ts`** — `resolveEmbeddingConnection()` (embeddings adapter bypasses the factory).
- **`src/engine/Orchestrator.ts`** — `localProviderFor()`/`cloudProviderFor()` routing classification (prevents comma-separated local URLs from being misclassified as cloud).

`engine/ModelRouter.ts` (interview-config endpoint router) was verified safe — its values are gated by `ConfigSerializer.validUrl()` at config-generation time, which already rejects comma-separated URLs.

### UI validation (visual feedback)
- **`src/settings/PluginSettingsTab.ts`** — live `input` listener on every Base URL field detects commas; reflects state on init and after the ↩ Reset button.
- **`src/styles.css`** — `.cc-url-input-invalid` (yellow border) and `.cc-url-warning` advisory line (`⚠ Multiple URLs detected. Only the first URL will be used for connections.`), hidden by default.

## Verification (all green)
- Typecheck: clean
- Lint: zero warnings
- Tests: **188/188 pass** (44 core + 144 react-suite); added section 33 with 6 new tests covering the helper, `BaseHttpProvider` wrapping, Anthropic/Gemini/Cohere/LM Studio endpoints, `ProviderFactory.getBaseUrl`, and `TranscriberAdapter`.
- `npm run build`: succeeds; new CSS classes confirmed in bundled `styles.css`.
- `npm run sanitize`: clean (123 files).
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- Benchmarks: within 25% gate (trace −26.7%, BM25 +11.8%, JSON −49.3%).

## Success criteria
- Input `http://10.5.0.2:1234, http://localhost:1234` → engine extracts and queries only `http://10.5.0.2:1234` at every network boundary (tested explicitly).
- Settings UI warns the user when multiple URLs are entered.
- Comma-separated inputs no longer produce malformed URI errors.
